summary: The root طفف (Tff) primarily means to give short measure or weight, to defraud in measuring or weighing, or to be deficient in doing so.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.gloss: was; became, near; I took, of my goods

parts.t: Take thou what has risen to thee, and become within thy power

headwords.def: طَفَّ , (As, O, K,) [aor., app., طَفِفَ ,] inf. n. طَفٌّ , (TK, [or, accord. to Freytag طُفُوفٌ , which see in what follows,]) It (a thing) was, or became, near. (As, O, K.) You say, أَخَذْتُ مِنْ مَتَاعِى مَا خَفَّ وَطَفَّ i. e. [ I took, of my goods, ] what [ was light, and ] was near to me. (As, O.) And طَفَّ الشَّىْءُ مِنَ الشَّىْءِ The thing was, or became, near to the thing. (O, K. *) And خُذْ مَا طَفَّ لَكَ , and لَكَ , (S, Meyd, O, K,) and لَكَ , (Meyd, O, TA,) Take thou what has risen to thee, and become within thy power or reach, (S, O, K, TA,) and become attainable [ to thee ], or prepared [ for thee ], (AZ, Meyd, TA,) and become near to thee: (K, TA:) or what has risen to view, and has appeared, [ to thee, ] to be taken: (TA:) [for] طَفَّ

headwords.gloss: He made defective; deficient; He gave short measure

parts.t: he made the contents of the measure to be defective,
(S, O, Msb, K,) and in like manner,
not filling the former to its uppermost parts:
he did thus, cheating his companion in measure
He scanted his household, stinted them,
He gave to the man less than he had taken from him.

headwords.def: طفّف He made defective, or deficient. (TA.) You say, طفّف , (K,) or طفّف المِكْيَالَ , and المِيزَانَ , (Msb,) inf. n. تَطْفِيفٌ , (S, O, Msb,) He gave short measure, and short weight; (Msb;) he made the contents of the measure to be defective, (S, O, Msb, K,) and in like manner, of the balance; (Msb;) not filling the former to its uppermost parts: (S, TA:) i. e. he did thus, cheating his companion in measure or in weight. (TA.) [Hence,] طفّف عَلَى عِيَالِهِ (tropical:) He scanted his household, stinted them, or was niggardly or parsimonious towards them, in expenditure. (TA.) And طفّف عَلَى الرَّجُلِ (assumed tropical:) He gave to the man less than he had taken from him. (TA.) And طفّف الإِنَآءَ He took what was upon [or above ] the vessel

headwords.def: طَفٌّ The side (O, K) of a thing: (O:) [like دَفٌّ :] and the bank, or shore, (O, K,) of a great river or a sea; (O;) as also : (O, K:) accord. to Lth, of the Euphrates: (O:) or, as some say, the elevated part of the side of the Euphrates. (TA.) And الطَّفُّ is applied to The part of the land of the Arabs that overlooks the cultivated region of El-'Irák: (IDrd, O, K:) said by As to be so called because it is near to the cultivated region: (O:) or it is a place in the district of El-Koofeh. (S, O, K. *) And The exterior court or yard of a house. (TA.) See also طَفَاف , in two places. And see طَفَّافٌ .

headwords.def: مُطَفِّفٌ One who gives short measure, and short weight, (Zj, Msb, TA,) thus cheating his companion; but this epithet is not applied unrestrictedly except in the case of exorbitant deficiency: [or] accord. to Aboo-Is-hák [i. e. Zj], the مطفّف is thus called because he seldom or never steals from the measure or balance save what is paltry, i. e. طَفِيف ; for it is from طَفُّ الشَّىْءِ , meaning “ the side of the thing: ” the pl. occurs in the Kur lxxxiii. 1. (TA.)
